title: Interim: borrow the serial port for flashing under conserver
description: Until OTA lands, conserver and espflash both want /dev/ttyUSB0 exclusively. Provide flash-under-conserver.sh (stop or down conserver, espflash flash, restore) wired as the cargo runner or a make target so cargo run transparently borrows the port; document conserver native down/up (Ctrl-E c d then o) as the lighter alternative. Superseded by the OTA epic once flashing no longer needs the UART.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] cargo run transparently borrows /dev/ttyUSB0 from conserver: stop/down, espflash, restore
- [ ] restore runs even when espflash FAILS (trap/finally); the flash-failure branch is tested and conserver comes back up
- [ ] manual fallback documented (conserver Ctrl-E c d, then o)
- [ ] retired when OTA fetch (qhw.23) lands

title: NightDriver-style WS2812 LED driver as an HA light
description: Second product on the shared foundation: a NightDriverStrip-inspired WS2812 effects driver for the workstation, exposed to Home Assistant as a Light entity (on/off, brightness, effect-select) through the same esphome-api framework. The existing led-core effects domain (color, effect, animator) is reused unchanged; under the std pivot the WS2812 adapter re-homes from esp-hal RMT to esp-idf-hal RMT. This epic proves the generic native-API entity framework pays off a second time: swap the adapter and expose a Light instead of a Sensor. Depends on the foundation (std pivot, workspace, esphome-api).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] HA controls the physical strip as a Light (on/off, brightness, effect select)
- [ ] led-core reused unchanged; only the WS2812 adapter re-homed to esp-idf RMT

title: led-driver bin: drive the WS2812 strip as an HA Light
description: The project #2 application binary: a composition root that drives the led-core effects through the re-homed WS2812 adapter and exposes the strip to Home Assistant as a Light entity (on/off, brightness, effect-select) via the esphome-api framework and the firmware-infra native-API server. Under Functional Core / Imperative Shell the animator returns a rendered frame value and the adapter (shell) writes it. Acceptance: HA shows a Light entity that toggles, dims, and switches effects on the physical strip. Depends on the WS2812 encoder, the Light entity type, and the native-API server infra.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] HA shows a Light entity that toggles, dims, and switches effects on the physical strip
- [ ] composition root wires animator -> frame value -> WS2812 adapter (FC/IS; shell complexity ~1)
- [ ] reuses firmware-infra server host + esphome-api unchanged (proves the framework generalizes)

title: esphome-api: add Light entity type to the registry
description: Extend the generic esphome-api entity model with a Light entity (on/off, brightness, effect-select): add the ListEntitiesLight, LightState, and LightCommand messages to the enums and implement a LightEntity mapping to led-core effect selection and brightness, including handle_command for inbound LightCommandRequest. Proves the framework generalizes beyond read-only Sensor. Tests: registry emits Light List/State; a LightCommand routes to the entity by key. Depends on the generic entity model.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Light variants added to the List/State/Command enums; LightEntity implements handle_command for LightCommandRequest
- [ ] maps to led-core effect selection + brightness
- [ ] tests: registry emits Light List/State; a LightCommand routes to the right entity by key; zero/one/many entities still enumerate; no Sensor regressions

title: std/ESP-IDF foundation + ESPHome-native plant monitor
description: Foundation plus first product. Pivot the M5StickC Plus firmware from no_std esp-hal to std on ESP-IDF (esp-idf-svc, esp-idf-hal, esp-idf-sys), then ship a soil-moisture plant monitor that appears to Home Assistant as a native ESPHome device (protobuf over TCP 6053 plus mDNS) so HA stores, graphs and alerts on the readings. Board is ESP32-PICO-D4 (4MB flash, 520KB SRAM, no PSRAM), which runs std comfortably. Why std: it turns the ESPHome native API into a roughly one-week job instead of weeks (std::net TCP, prost protobuf, ESP-IDF WiFi/mDNS/OTA, pure-Rust Noise) and it also simplifies OTA. Domain crates (led-core, plant-core, the esphome-api protocol core) stay pure and framework-free. Architecture: hexagonal/ECB plus Functional Core / Imperative Shell (Bernhardt Boundaries) plus dogfooding the ~/code/tools contract suite (hex-lint, effect-audit, cargo-regime-check) as the CI gates that enforce both. This epic reverses and supersedes the no_std OTA epic stick-c-plus-qqh (ESP-IDF supplies WiFi/OTA/mDNS natively). MVP milestone is the plaintext native-API sensor entity graphing in HA. Full design saved at docs/plans/plant-monitor-esphome-native-api.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] MVP: Soil Moisture graphs in HA History and a watering alert fires (qhw.22 closed)
- [ ] the native-API framework is generic: fmz adds a Light entity without rewriting (fmz.2 lands on it cleanly)
- [ ] architecture gates green and proven fail-able: hex-lint, effect-audit --require-domain, cargo-regime-check

title: Stand up the std/ESP-IDF build and boot
description: Get the firmware crate building and BOOTING on std ESP-IDF, nothing more. Target xtensa-esp32-espidf on the esp toolchain; add esp-idf-svc 0.52, esp-idf-hal 0.46, esp-idf-sys 0.37; linker via ldproxy; build-std = std,panic_abort; build.rs uses embuild sysenv output; add sdkconfig.defaults (larger main-task and pthread stacks, more lwIP sockets, mDNS max services, size optimization); pin ESP_IDF_VERSION to a 5.3.x tag (esp-idf-sys 0.37 needs at least 5.3.0). Drop esp-hal, esp-backtrace, esp-println. Runner stays espflash flash --monitor; ELF path becomes target/xtensa-esp32-espidf. SCOPE: only a minimal std binary that boots and logs over serial. Re-homing the WS2812 and Clock adapters and the workspace split are separate beads. Acceptance: a minimal std ESP-IDF binary flashes and logs on the board. Open item: confirm the exact 5.3.x tag esp-idf-sys 0.37 targets.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] cargo build --release on the esp toolchain produces target/xtensa-esp32-espidf/release/<bin> (ELF)
- [ ] espflash flashes it; serial shows the ESP-IDF boot banner plus a log line from our fn main()
- [ ] no boot loop: the device runs 60s+ past main() with no repeated reset (the rst: cause line does not recur)
- [ ] ESP_IDF_VERSION pinned to an exact v5.3.x tag in .cargo/config.toml; the minimum-IDF floor verified from the esp-idf-sys 0.37 changelog, not hearsay
- [ ] esp-hal, esp-backtrace, esp-println absent from cargo tree
- [ ] sdkconfig.defaults committed AND effective: the GENERATED sdkconfig in the build output shows the intended CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS / CONFIG_MDNS_MAX_SERVICES / stack values (a mistyped key is silently ignored — proof it took effect, not that the line exists)

title: Noise encryption follow-on for the native API
description: Add the Noise transport so the native API is encrypted, matching current ESPHome direction (2026.1 removed API password auth from ESPHome YAML — a firmware-compiler constraint; the HA client itself still accepts plaintext). Reuse the UbiHome noise-protocol plus noise-rust-crypto responder (no_std-capable, no tokio; Unlicense = MIT-compatible): Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256, PSK is the base64 32-byte HA key, device is the responder. PURITY: the responder's ephemeral key needs a CSPRNG — inject randomness from the shell as a value/port (or host the handshake in firmware-infra) so the role=domain core stays RNG-free and effect-audit holds. Feature-gate so plaintext builds omit it. Advertise api_encryption in the mDNS TXT when on. On the HA side, paste the same base64 key into the ESPHome integration. Open items: confirm noise crates cross-compile on xtensa-esp32-espidf; verify the Noise inner-frame layout against aioesphomeapi connection.py.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256, device = responder, PSK = base64 32-byte HA key
- [ ] randomness injected from the shell (value/port) or handshake hosted in firmware-infra — the role=domain core stays RNG-free and effect-audit stays green
- [ ] HA (or aioesphomeapi with the key) connects encrypted; a wire capture shows 0x01 frames with no readable plaintext (no silent fallback)
- [ ] wrong key, wrong-LENGTH key, truncated/replayed handshake: clean rejection, connection closed, no panic
- [ ] plaintext builds exclude all noise deps via feature gate (cargo tree proves)
- [ ] mDNS TXT advertises api_encryption when on
- [ ] per-connection stack high-water re-measured with Noise linked; stack_size raised if the plaintext budget no longer holds
- [ ] Open items resolved: noise crates cross-compile on xtensa; inner-frame layout verified against aioesphomeapi connection.py

title: Stand up Home Assistant on the LAN
description: Home Assistant is the store-and-graph plane for every project and is not yet running. Stand up an instance on the LAN: HAOS on a mini-PC, Pi, or VM is recommended; HA Container (Docker) also works but must use host networking or macvlan so mDNS discovery works on the same L2. No MQTT or Mosquitto needed on the native-API path. SCOPE: only a reachable HA; adopting the device is a separate bead. Acceptance: HA is reachable on the LAN. Can start immediately, independent of the firmware.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] HA reachable at a stable LAN URL; onboarding complete; Recorder storing history
- [ ] HA host sits on the same L2 as the device (Container: host networking or macvlan); an mDNS browse works from it
- [ ] decision recorded: HAOS vs Container, and why

title: ESP-IDF OTA slot mechanism (EspOta: write, flip, rollback)
description: The OTA mechanism on ESP-IDF: use esp-idf-svc EspOta to write an image into the inactive OTA slot, mark it, reboot into it, and roll back on a failed boot. ESP-IDF supplies the partition, otadata, and bootloader machinery natively (why this supersedes the whole no_std OTA stack the old qqh epic pinned). SCOPE: only the local slot mechanism (image source may be an embedded blob or flash read here); the network fetch and update policy are a separate bead. Acceptance: an image is written to the inactive slot, booted, and a deliberately bad image rolls back, on the board. Depends on the std build and the workspace.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] partition table sized from the MEASURED release image (qhw.28 records it): two app slots + otadata fit 4 MB with a stated margin
- [ ] EspOta writes an image to the inactive slot, marks it, reboots into it (new version visible in the boot log)
- [ ] a checksum-corrupt image rolls back via the bootloader
- [ ] an image that BOOTS but fails its self-test triggers app-initiated rollback (mark-invalid path)
- [ ] power loss mid-slot-write leaves the device booting the prior good slot with intact otadata
- [ ] no network in this bead (fetch is qhw.23)

title: Pin ESPHome/ESP-IDF reference sources to kb/sources
description: Save the reference material offline (user request) as pinned kb/sources entries (commit/tag pinned submodules or fetched datasheets): UbiHome/esphome-native-api plus its encryption doc; aioesphomeapi (the api.proto source and connection.py Noise oracle); a note that esphome/esphome components/api is GPLv3 and reference-only; ESPHome native-API protocol details; HA ESPHome integration and security/Noise pages; the Rust-on-ESP std book, esp-idf-template, esp-idf-sys build options; esp-idf-svc and esp-idf-hal docs; prost, noise-protocol, noise-rust-crypto and the Noise NNpsk0 spec; mipidsi, embedded-graphics and the ST7789 datasheet; axp192 and the AXP192 datasheet; the Earth Unit datasheet. SCOPE: pinning sources only; writing the derived findings is a separate bead. Depends on the vendored crate being chosen.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] every source listed in the bead pinned under kb/sources with commit/tag + license noted
- [ ] esphome/esphome marked GPLv3 REFERENCE-ONLY, never copy
- [ ] kb index updated so the sources are discoverable

title: Tag crates with hex-arch roles + wire hex-lint gate
description: Tag every workspace crate with package.metadata.hex-arch role (domain / driven-adapter / infra / composition-root) and optional context (led / plant / api), then wire the hex-lint gate (from ~/code/tools) into the justfile and pre-commit/CI. It fails any cross-role dependency edge, for example the ESPHome transport or the ADC HAL sneaking into a role=domain crate. Advisory first, then blocking; follow the suite exit-code contract 0 clean / 1 policy violation / 2 tool error. Also adopt the suite house style: forbid unsafe on our crates, clippy deny-all, cucumber specs. SCOPE: role tagging plus hex-lint only; effect-audit and cargo-regime-check are separate beads. Depends on the workspace skeleton.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] every crate in both workspaces tagged [package.metadata.hex-arch] role (+context on the domain crates)
- [ ] hex-lint wired into justfile + pre-commit/CI, advisory first
- [ ] exit-code contract exercised BOTH ways: an induced tool error (exit 2) turns the pipeline red — never treated as clean
- [ ] gate proven able to FAIL AND RECOVER: a seeded cross-role dep is caught (exit 1), removed, and the re-run is green (exit 0); the seed never lands in a commit
- [ ] house style on our crates: #![forbid(unsafe_code)], clippy deny warnings

title: Re-home the Clock adapter to std/ESP-IDF time
description: Re-implement the led-core Clock port adapter (currently EspClock over the esp-hal monotonic timer) on ESP-IDF time (esp-idf-hal or std Instant), returning elapsed Duration from boot. Small shell adapter in the adapters crate. Under Functional Core / Imperative Shell the shell reads the clock and passes the value into the domain. Acceptance: the animator/sampler receives correct monotonic time on the board. Depends on the std build and the workspace skeleton.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clock adapter returns monotonic Duration since boot on ESP-IDF
- [ ] rate verified, not just monotonicity: elapsed matches a known wall-clock interval within a stated tolerance (catches a us-vs-ms scale bug that monotonicity alone passes)
- [ ] led-core Animator ticks with steady progression on the board
- [ ] lives in the adapters crate; the shell reads the clock, the domain receives a value

title: plant-core: SoilSensor port + pure sampler step
description: Add to plant-core the driven port SoilSensor (associated Error, read_raw returning 0..=4095) and the PURE Control step: given previous state, a slice of raw readings, and Calibration, average, calibrate (via to_percent), and return the new state plus whether the value changed. No sensor handle, no caching, no I/O in the core. Tests: unit tests with a scripted-sensor fake (zero/one/many readings); a cucumber feature moisture.feature (given calibration and a reading, then a percent). effect-audit must pass with role=domain. Depends on the Moisture/calibration bead. Pure host work.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] SoilSensor trait: associated Error; read_raw -> 0..=4095 documented
- [ ] step(prev, raw, cal) is pure: no I/O, no clock, no interior mutability; deterministic
- [ ] tests cover zero readings (no report), one, many — and the many case uses inputs where mean != first != last != min != max (e.g. [10,20,60] -> exactly 30) so a non-averaging impl FAILS
- [ ] unchanged value -> None, changed -> Some(Moisture)
- [ ] cucumber moisture.feature runs under cargo test ([[test]] harness = false)
- [ ] effect-audit role=domain passes once the gate is wired (qhw.25)
close_reason: Implemented and verified on host; see comment.

title: esphome-api: blocking frame codec over std::io
description: Implement the ESPHome native-API frame codec as a blocking reader/writer over std::io Read and Write, replacing the vendored tokio-util codec. Plaintext frame = 1-byte preamble 0x00, then varint payload-size, then varint message-type-id, then exactly payload-size bytes of protobuf — ONE length field, size BEFORE type (verified against developers.esphome.io protocol details and aioesphomeapi). Encrypted frames (preamble 0x01, 2-byte big-endian length) are handled by the Noise bead. Keep the byte-level encode/decode pure over buffers; the std::io pump is a thin wrapper, so the effect-audit domain boundary stays meaningful. Tests: golden known-answer frames captured from aioesphomeapi (round-trip alone only proves self-consistency), round-trip properties, malformed and short-read handling. Depends on the vendored crate and proto types.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] plaintext framing matches the REAL wire: 0x00, varint payload-size, varint message-type, payload — size before type, ONE length field (per developers.esphome.io + aioesphomeapi)
- [ ] known-answer test: encoding a fixed message is byte-exact against a CAPTURED aioesphomeapi plaintext frame, and decoding that captured frame yields the message (round-trip alone only proves self-consistency)
- [ ] round-trip property test across sizes: empty, 1-byte, many-byte payloads and varint length boundaries
- [ ] malformed preamble, truncated frame, oversized length -> typed errors, never a panic
- [ ] preamble 0x01 (encrypted) recognized and cleanly rejected until the Noise bead (qhw.10)
- [ ] byte-level encode/decode is pure over buffers; the std::io pump is a thin wrapper (keeps the effect-audit domain boundary meaningful)
close_reason: Plaintext frame codec landed: pure frame.rs encode/decode + thin frame_io.rs std::io pump. Known-answer test against CAPTURED aioesphomeapi frames (byte-exact both ways), proptest round-trip across sizes/varint boundaries, typed errors for bad preamble/oversized/truncated (never panics), preamble 0x01 rejected for the Noise bead. 34 tests + clippy clean. Commit 9c00805.

title: esphome-api: generic entity model (ApiEntity + Registry + Sensor)
description: Define the generic entity abstraction: an ApiEntity trait (key, object_id, list_message, state_message, handle_command) and a Registry holding boxed entities, with List/State/Command enums covering every ESPHome entity type (Sensor, BinarySensor, Switch, Light, Number, Select, Cover). Implement SensorEntity now; other types are enum variants added later without rewrite. Pure. Tests: registry enumerates List and State messages for a Sensor; key hashing is stable. Depends on the vendored crate and proto types.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] ApiEntity trait (key, object_id, list_message, state_message, handle_command) + Registry of boxed entities
- [ ] SensorEntity implemented; List/State/Command enums cover Sensor|BinarySensor|Switch|Light|Number|Select|Cover — non-Sensor variants documented as UNVERIFIED placeholders until an entity of that type ships and passes the oracle
- [ ] key uses a deterministic, documented hash (ESPHome uses fnv1a; NOT std DefaultHasher/RandomState) — the snapshot value is reproduced by a freshly-spawned process, so keys are reboot-stable and HA entities never churn
- [ ] registry enumeration tested for zero, one, many entities
- [ ] new-entity-type recipe (enum variant + prost message + match arm, no rewrite) documented in the crate
close_reason: Entity model landed: ApiEntity trait (key/object_id/list_message/state_message/handle_command) + Registry (boxed entities, zero/one/many enumeration, key-routed apply_command). List/State/Command enums cover Sensor|BinarySensor|Switch|Light|Number|Select|Cover; only Sensor implemented, rest are documented UNVERIFIED placeholders (add variant+arm+impl, no rewrite). Wire ids resolve via MESSAGE_IDS. Keys = seedless FNV-1a over object_id UTF-8 (reboot-stable, NOT DefaultHasher) checked against an independent Python oracle. clippy clean. Commit 960048f.

title: esphome-api: pure connection FSM + host value-tests
description: Implement the native-API connection as a PURE function of state and inbound message: handle(conn, inbound, entity-snapshot) returns (new-conn, outbound-messages). Cover Hello, DeviceInfo, ListEntities plus ListEntitiesDone, SubscribeStates then stream states, Ping/Pong, Disconnect. No sockets. Tests (Functional Core, no network, no mocks): feed inbound frames as values and assert the outbound sequence and every entity List/State message; include an integration test that binds 127.0.0.1 and drives the real aioesphomeapi client as a conformance oracle. effect-audit must pass with role=domain. Depends on the codec and the entity model.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] handle(conn, inbound, snapshot) -> (conn, Vec<OutboundMsg>) is pure; no sockets in the core
- [ ] covers Hello, ConnectRequest/ConnectResponse (HA sends it right after Hello even on plaintext), DeviceInfo, ListEntities + Done, SubscribeStates + state stream, Ping/Pong, Disconnect
- [ ] value-tests assert full outbound sequences, including out-of-order/unexpected inbound
- [ ] integration test binds 127.0.0.1 and the REAL aioesphomeapi client ASSERTS values: device_info fields match, the entity list matches exactly, subscribe observes 2+ DISTINCT states — mere completion is not a pass
- [ ] effect-audit role=domain passes for the core once the gate is wired
close_reason: Pure connection FSM landed + VERIFIED against the real aioesphomeapi client. handle(conn,inbound,snapshot)->(conn,Vec<Outbound>) is pure (no sockets); covers Hello, Authentication (plaintext connect), DeviceInfo, ListEntities+Done, SubscribeStates+state stream, Ping/Pong, Disconnect; broadcast_states gated on active subscription. Value-tests assert full outbound sequences incl zero/one/many + out-of-order/unknown. Integration oracle (tests/aioesphomeapi_oracle.rs + ha_client_oracle.py) binds 127.0.0.1 and drives the REAL HA client which asserts device_info name, exact entity list, 2+ distinct states — passed. effect-audit --strict role=domain clean; gate wired via 'just audit'. Commit a5e7a28.

title: Carve the firmware into a multi-crate workspace
description: Split the firmware into a workspace of small single-responsibility crates so the hexagon and Functional-Core/Imperative-Shell boundaries become enforceable per crate. New members: board-support (M5StickC Plus BSP, reused by all projects); firmware-infra (WiFi, mDNS, the native-API socket server host, OTA; reused by all projects); adapters (domain-port adapters: adc, st7789, wifi, clock, ws2812); bins/plant-monitor (first binary and composition root). Shared host crates (led-core, plant-core, esphome-api) referenced by path. Move the existing composition root into bins/plant-monitor. SCOPE: only the crate skeleton and moving existing code in. The hex-arch role tags and the CI gates are a separate bead. Acceptance: the workspace builds and the layout matches the design. Depends on the std build.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] firmware workspace members exist and build: board-support, firmware-infra, adapters, bins/plant-monitor
- [ ] existing composition root moved to bins/plant-monitor; the minimal binary still flashes and logs
- [ ] host crates (domain/led-core, plant-core, esphome-api) referenced by path across workspaces
- [ ] each crate declares exactly one hex-arch role (mechanical enforcement lands with qhw.14); NO gates yet (qhw.14/25/26)

title: AXP192 power-on (board-support): enable LCD/TFT rails
description: In the board-support crate, bring up the internal I2C bus (SDA GPIO21, SCL GPIO22) and power the AXP192 PMIC rails the board needs: LDO2 (LCD backlight) and LDO3 (TFT), plus the standard M5StickC Plus init register writes to address 0x34. Load-bearing prerequisite for the display; reused by every project. Share the one I2C bus via embedded-hal-bus (AXP192 now, MPU6886/RTC later). Acceptance: the backlight powers on and the AXP192 reports the expected rail voltages. Depends on the std build and the workspace skeleton.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] internal I2C up (SDA 21, SCL 22); AXP192 answers at 0x34
- [ ] LDO2/LDO3 enabled via the standard M5StickC Plus init sequence; backlight visibly on
- [ ] read-back rail voltages match expected values
- [ ] bus shared via embedded-hal-bus so MPU6886/RTC can coexist later

title: Sampler shell thread: ADC to plant-core step to shared Moisture
description: The imperative-shell sampler: a sized std::thread that periodically reads the ADC adapter, runs the pure plant-core sampler step, and publishes the latest Moisture into a shared Arc Mutex that the display and the native-API server read. Owns the timing and the cache (the core stays pure). Acceptance: the shared latest-Moisture updates on the board as the probe wets and dries. Depends on the ADC adapter and the pure sampler step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] dedicated std::thread with explicit stack_size; sample period is a named constant
- [ ] publishes the latest Moisture WITH a timestamp into the shared slot read by display + server
- [ ] staleness is fail-visible: a value older than N sample periods surfaces as None/unavailable to consumers; a test that kills the sampler flips the served state to unavailable within N periods — a dead sensor must never keep reporting its last healthy value
- [ ] panic-safe sharing: an injected ADC error or forced sampler panic neither poisons the shared state nor crashes the server thread (lock recovery or supervised restart, proven by test)
- [ ] all averaging/calibration goes through the pure plant-core step (no domain logic in the shell; complexity ~1)
- [ ] on board: the shared value tracks probe dry -> wet within one sample period

title: Adopt the device in HA + moisture graph + watering alert
description: With Home Assistant running and the device serving the native API, adopt it: accept the mDNS discovery or add the ESPHome integration by IP on port 6053 (plaintext: no key; Noise: paste the base64 key). Confirm the Soil Moisture entity records history and graphs. Add a watering-alert automation that fires when the moisture entity crosses a low threshold. Acceptance: the entity graphs in HA History and the alert fires on a dry reading. Depends on standing up HA and the on-device server MVP.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] device adopted in HA (mDNS discovery accepted or manual add via IP:6053)
- [ ] History graph shows VARIATION correlated with real wet/dry transitions over hours — a frozen flat line is a failure, not a pass
- [ ] watering alert: stays SILENT on wet soil, FIRES when moisture crosses the low threshold (probe into air), and RE-ARMS — fires again on a second dry cycle after re-wetting
- [ ] soak 24h+: still adopted, no update gap over N minutes, value still tracking real changes, and end free-heap within a stated margin of start (no slow leak)

title: OTA image fetch + update use case (HTTP pull, policy, trigger)
description: On top of the OTA slot mechanism, add the update use case: fetch a firmware image over WiFi (HTTP pull from a homelab URL) and drive the slot write/flip/rollback. Model the update policy (whether/when to update, version check) in the domain and the HTTP transport as an adapter. Acceptance: an image served from the homelab is pulled and booted end to end. Depends on the OTA slot mechanism and WiFi. Once this lands, the interim serial-borrow bead stick-c-plus-5ww is retired and the UART can host a permanent shared console.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] update policy (version compare, whether/when to update) modeled in a domain crate; HTTP transport is an adapter
- [ ] an image served from a homelab URL is fetched, written via the slot mechanism, and booted end-to-end
- [ ] a failed download or bad image never bricks the device: rollback proven
- [ ] follow-up recorded: retire stick-c-plus-5ww once this lands

title: Write kb/findings for the pivot, native API, Noise, Earth Unit, pin map
description: Write the derived KB findings (one falsifiable fact per file): the std/ESP-IDF pivot that supersedes the no_std OTA stack (cross-link the esp-rs version matrix); the ESPHome native-API framing (plaintext: 0x00, varint size, varint type — NOT 2-byte length) plus message-type-id table plus connection flow; the ESPHome Noise parameters (NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256, device is responder); the Earth Unit RESISTIVE probe on ADC1 channel 5 (G33) — not corrosion-resistant, power-gated sampling — with dry/wet calibration and the ADC1-for-WiFi-coexistence rule; the M5StickC Plus std-ESP-IDF pin map. Depends on the MVP server so the findings reflect verified behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] one falsifiable fact per file; each states what was verified on hardware vs read in docs
- [ ] findings exist: std-pivot supersession, native-API framing + type-id table + connection flow, Noise params, Earth Unit ADC1/G33 + calibration, std pin map
- [ ] superseded banner added to kb/findings/esp-rs-ota-version-matrix.md, cross-linked both ways

title: Wire effect-audit --require-domain over the domain crates
description: Add the effect-audit gate (from ~/code/tools) to the justfile and pre-commit/CI over the Functional-Core crates led-core, plant-core, and the esphome-api core. It fails the instant a clock, RNG, ADC handle, socket, tokio, or mutable-static leaks into a role=domain crate. Use --require-domain as the anti-false-green guard (a run that audited nothing exits 2). Advisory first, then blocking. Feedback loop: effect-audit is the least-productized of the six tools, so leaning on it here will surface and harden its rough edges. Depends on the hex-arch role tagging and the domain crates existing.
acceptance_criteria:

title: Soil calibration: capture dry/wet points + persist to NVS
description: Make the moisture percent MEANINGFUL. Soil probes vary per unit and drift (the resistive Earth pads also corrode), so dry_raw/wet_raw must be captured per probe, not hardcoded. Add a device-side calibration flow: capture a dry reading (probe in air/dry soil) and a wet reading (probe in water/wet soil), triggered by the ON-BOARD BUTTON (BtnA G37 / BtnB G39); an HA Button/Number-entity trigger is out of scope until the registry grows those entity types. Persist the Calibration to ESP-IDF NVS so it survives reboot; the sampler reads the persisted calibration. NVS writes must be power-loss-safe (a torn write must never produce a degenerate pair — pairs with plant-core's defined dry==wet behavior). The raw MVP may ship with hardcoded constants; this refines it into a usable monitor.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] dry + wet capture triggered by the ON-BOARD button writes Calibration to NVS (an HA Button/Number-entity trigger is deferred until those entity types exist in the registry)
- [ ] calibration survives a clean power cycle; the sampler uses the persisted values
- [ ] power-loss-safe: an interrupted NVS write leaves the previous calibration or safe defaults, never a corrupt/degenerate pair; boot with corrupted/zeroed NVS falls back to defaults without panic (pairs with plant-core's defined dry==wet behavior)
- [ ] partial capture handled: dry captured but wet not yet -> defined behavior, no bogus percent
- [ ] after capture: ~0% in the dry state, ~100% in the wet state; both probe orderings handled

title: plant-core: Moisture entity + calibration (pure)

Degenerate calibration (dry_raw == wet_raw, e.g. zeroed NVS) must return a defined value, never divide by zero. Tests: property tests proving the result is always in 0..=100, dry_raw maps to 0, wet_raw maps to 100, monotonicity, out-of-range clamps. The SoilSensor port and the sampler step are a separate bead. effect-audit must pass with role=domain. Pure host work; start immediately.

- [ ] plant-core is no_std, zero-dependency, #![forbid(unsafe_code)]

- [ ] to_percent is integer-only i32 math (no float, no libm), clamped
- [ ] proptests: result always 0..=100 for any (raw, cal); dry_raw->0; wet_raw->100; monotone between; clamps outside; BOTH calibration orders handled (resistive Earth probe expected wet-high, but the math must not assume a direction)
- [ ] degenerate calibration defined: dry_raw == wet_raw (e.g. zeroed NVS) returns a defined value, no panic/divide-by-zero; the proptest generator explicitly covers equal and adjacent endpoints

title: Gate Earth-probe power: energize only during sampling
description: The Earth Unit is a RESISTIVE soil probe; m5 docs state the electrodes are not anti-corrosive, POC-grade, and should not sit in a humid environment for long. Constant DC bias across the exposed pads electrolyzes them — a 24/7 plant monitor corrodes the probe and drifts the calibration within weeks. Energize the probe only during a sampling window and keep it unpowered between samples. Candidate mechanisms (implementer's choice): gate the Grove 5V rail via the AXP192 boost/EXTEN path in board-support, a GPIO-driven high-side switch, or duty-cycled sampling with an empirically-determined settle delay before each read. The pure plant-core step stays untouched — gating is shell work in the sampler/adapter. Found by cross-model review (2026-07-03); sources: docs.m5stack.com/en/unit/earth, shop.m5stack.com Earth listing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] probe is unpowered between samples (verified at the Grove 5V pin or via AXP192 state)
- [ ] settle delay after power-on determined empirically; gated readings match always-on readings within a stated tolerance
- [ ] duty cycle documented (powered window vs sample period)
- [ ] gating lives in the shell; the pure plant-core step is untouched

title: ADC adapter: SoilSensor over ADC1 on GPIO33
description: Shell adapter implementing the plant-core SoilSensor port over the ESP-IDF oneshot ADC. Read the Earth Unit analog output on GPIO33, which is ADC1 channel 5. The Earth Unit is a RESISTIVE probe (two exposed pads as a variable divider — wet conducts more; per m5 docs the electrodes are not corrosion-resistant, hence the separate probe-power-gating bead). MUST be ADC1, because ADC2 is unusable while WiFi is active. Use esp-idf-hal AdcDriver on ADC1 plus an AdcChannelDriver on gpio33 with 12 dB attenuation; oversample and average. Error type is EspError. The digital threshold line on GPIO32 is optional and could later back a BinarySensor entity. Confirmed by the vendor Earth example in the repo which does analogRead(33). Open item: whether esp-idf-hal 0.46 exposes ADC line/curve calibration on ESP32 (raw counts are adequate for relative moisture regardless).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] implements the plant-core SoilSensor port; type Error = EspError
- [ ] reads ADC1 ch5 / GPIO33 at 12 dB attenuation; oversampled mean of N samples (N documented)
- [ ] on board WITH WIFI CONNECTED: dry air / dry soil / wet soil raw counts are consistently monotonically ordered with a stated minimum gap; the direction is recorded (resistive probe expected wet-high) — a wrongly-used ADC2 would fail this while WiFi is up
- [ ] oversampled reading spread stays within a stated band at constant moisture
- [ ] Open item resolved: note whether esp-idf-hal 0.46 exposes ADC calibration on ESP32

title: OTA-over-WiFi firmware updates

Board is confirmed capable: ESP32-PICO-D4, 2.4GHz WiFi, 4MB flash; the factory partition table already carries otadata and the ESP-IDF second-stage bootloader honors A/B OTA slots. Target stack pinned to latest (mid-2026): esp-hal 1.1, esp-radio (WiFi, successor to esp-wifi), esp-rtos (scheduler, successor to esp-hal-embassy), esp-storage plus esp-bootloader-esp-idf (flash writes plus otadata/rollback), embassy-net (TCP). Endgame: images push over the network into the inactive OTA slot and the UART is freed for a permanent shared console. led-core stays framework-free; OTA is a new use case behind ports. See the KB finding on the esp-rs version/compat matrix.

The transport is an adapter; the update policy (whether/when to update, version check) lives in the domain. Acceptance: an image served from the homelab is pulled and booted end-to-end, and a deliberately-bad image rolls back.
